newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds continue slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds continue slightly lower.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed nearly unchanged with a negative trend on Tuesday with prices of CPI-linked bonds continuing to decline but at a more gradual rate, traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.03 to 105.43
Volume including Makams was 130 million shekels.
"One can say that trading today was a continuation of the trend yesterday but on a weaker scale," said a trader at the investment department of one of the big banks.

"There is still a negative trend to the CPI-linked bonds because of the lower than expected (April) consumer price index (CPI). But for a very small part of these bonds there was big demand because they offered high yields of 4.40 percent. During trading this yield was lowered to 4.15 percent," he said.

"Now the market is on a see-saw about interest rates. Some believe the Bank of Israel will cut interest rates some don't. In any case the prices of bonds already reflect a small cut in the interest rates," the trader said.

April's 0.7 percent CPI rise, published on Thursday, was well below analysts' forecasts of about 1.1 percent. The Bank of Israel will publish its key lending rate for June on May 26. The central bank last cut its interest rate to 13.9 percent at the end of February.

"The market today reached a balance again. Today there was some correction to the price falls yesterday. The market expects inflation to be lower in the coming months and the price rises in unlinked bonds continued but at a lower rate," said a trader at a big portfolio management company.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
